description: A venue operations director must approve the operating plan for a film festival premiere, including the venue, audience capacity, insurance filing, and post-screening guest appearance.

shared_context.S1: The festival's premiere screening is scheduled for Saturday evening at the Riverside Courtyard, with the Harbor Hall available as an alternate venue.
shared_context.S2: The courtyard has been advertised as the premiere location, while Harbor Hall is licensed for festival screenings.
shared_context.S3: Mara has final authority to approve the operating plan and audience admission for the screening.
shared_context.S4: Under the festival's normal pre-opening routine, Mara checks with production, insurance, and talent coordination before approving the final plan.
shared_context.S5: The screening is followed by a moderated audience question-and-answer session with the film's lead guest.

PF1.text: Jonah's production safety check found that the courtyard screen rig is rated for sustained wind up to 18 mph, while the Saturday forecast is 22 mph; Harbor Hall has a certified indoor rig and a maximum audience capacity of 600. Jonah completed the check this morning but has not yet entered the result in the shared production log.

PF2.text: Leila confirmed with the insurer today that the event policy covers the screening only if the certificate of insurance naming the festival and Harbor Hall is filed before doors open; the certificate for the courtyard does not satisfy that endorsement. She received the insurer's written confirmation but has not uploaded it to the venue file.

PF3.text: Sofia confirmed with the lead guest's agent this afternoon that the guest is available for the question-and-answer session only from 7:45 PM to 8:10 PM, so the session must begin at exactly 7:45 PM. The agent's confirmation is still in Sofia's email and has not been added to the festival schedule.

acceptance_conditions: The premiere must be moved to Harbor Hall.
Audience admission must be capped at exactly 600 people.
The Harbor Hall insurance certificate must be filed before doors open.
The question-and-answer session must begin at exactly 7:45 PM.
Technical relocation, insurance filing, and guest scheduling commitments must be logged.
The production safety finding must be cited by the decision-maker.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'technical_relocation' and c['target'] == 'Harbor Hall' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'insurance_certificate' and c['target'] == 'Harbor Hall' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'guest_schedule' and c['target'] == 'lead guest' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The 22 mph forecast makes the courtyard rig unsafe and changes the venue to Harbor Hall, whose exact safe audience capacity is 600, while requiring a technical relocation commitment.
The insurer's endorsement changes the required filing from a generic venue certificate to a Harbor Hall certificate filed before doors open and requires an insurance commitment.
The lead guest's confirmed 7:45 PM to 8:10 PM window changes the question-and-answer start time to exactly 7:45 PM and requires a guest-scheduling commitment.
